name: AZD-1940
summary: 13 or NEO-1940, is a drug developed by AstraZeneca, that is a peripherally selective cannabinoid agonist which binds with high affinity to both the cannabinoid CB1 and CB2 receptors.

pharmacology.text: AZD-1940, also known as ART27.13 or NEO-1940, is a drug developed by AstraZeneca, that is a peripherally selective cannabinoid agonist which binds with high affinity to both the cannabinoid CB1 and CB2 receptors.

uses.text: AZD-1940, also known as ART27.13 or NEO-1940, is a drug developed by AstraZeneca, that is a peripherally selective cannabinoid agonist which binds with high affinity to both the cannabinoid CB1 and CB2 receptors.

sideEffects.en: In trials the reported effects included dizziness, dry mouth and feeling intoxicated despite its peripheral design. It never reached the market, so its long-term effects are not known.
sideEffects.zh: 在試驗中回報的反應包括頭暈、口乾，以及儘管設計為外周作用仍出現的醉態感。它從未上市，因此長期影響不明。
sideEffects.zhHans: 在试验中回报的反应包括头晕、口干，以及尽管设计为外周作用仍出现的醉态感。它从未上市，因此长期影响不明。

fact.en: AstraZeneca designed it to stay out of the brain, the aim being cannabinoid pain relief without intoxication. In trials that separation did not hold up well enough for it to go on.
fact.zh: 阿斯特捷利康設計它留在腦外，目的是取得大麻素的止痛效果而不產生醉態。但在試驗中，這種分離效果不夠理想，開發因此未能繼續。
fact.zhHans: 阿斯特捷利康设计它留在脑外，目的是取得大麻素的止痛效果而不产生醉态。但在试验中，这种分离效果不够理想，开发因此未能继续。
